title: A weakly etale algebra over a field is reduced, integral, a filtered colimit of finite separable products, and closed under subalgebras, quotients and tensor products

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterisation of weakly etale algebras over a field as reduced algebras integral over the field whose finitely generated subalgebras are etale
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the criterion that turns the finitely generated description into weak etaleness for subalgebras.

standard_prerequisites.name: Etale K-algebras as finite products of finite separable extensions of K
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the shape of the finitely generated subalgebras and of the quotients whose colimits are taken.

standard_prerequisites.name: Permanence of weak etaleness under base change and composition

core_obligations: Deduce part (1), that B is reduced, from the absolutely-flat-over-absolutely-flat lemma, noting it also follows from part (3) (proof lines 30862-30863).
Deduce part (3) from the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma together with the fact that etale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions of K (proof lines 30864-30867).
Derive part (2) from part (3), and part (4) from (3) using that a product of fields is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents (proof lines 30868-30870).
Part (5), subalgebras: show that a subalgebra S is the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subalgebras, each etale over K by part (3), hence S is weakly etale over K (proof lines 30873-30877).

Part (5), quotients: show that a quotient Q is the filtered colimit of quotients of finite products of finite separable extensions, that such a quotient is of the form prod_{i in J} L_i for a subset J, and conclude by the same reasoning (proof lines 30878-30883).
Part (6): conclude that B tensor_K B' is weakly etale over K, either by the same reasoning or by combining the base change and composition permanence lemmas (proof lines 30886-30888).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six structural properties of a K-algebra B that is weakly etale over a field K: that B is reduced; that B is integral over K; that every finitely generated K-subalgebra of B is a finite product of finite separable extensions of K; that B is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents, in which case it is a separable algebraic extension of K; that every subalgebra or quotient algebra of B is again weakly etale over K; and that the tensor product of two such algebras is again weakly etale (source lines 30845-30859). The proof assembles these from the two preceding results and from the structure of etale algebras over a field. Part (1) is drawn from the absolutely-flat-over-absolutely-flat lemma. Part (3) follows from the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma together with the fact that etale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions (proof lines 30861-30867). Part (3) implies (2), and part (4) follows from (3) because a product of fields is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents (proof lines 30868-30870). The substantive part is (5): for a subalgebra S of B the proof observes that S is the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subalgebras, each of which is etale over K by the above, and hence S is weakly etale by the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma; for a quotient B -> Q the proof uses that Q is the filtered colimit of quotients of finite products of finite separable extensions, and that any quotient of such a product is itself a sub-product, so the result follows by the same reasoning (proof lines 30873-30883). Part (6) is then obtained either similarly or by combining the base change and composition permanence lemmas (proof lines 30886-30888). The non-routine content is the filtered-colimit argument for subalgebras and the sub-product description of quotients of finite separable products.
